detailed_description: The Salary Calculator is a precision tool for converting compensation across different pay periods using standardized financial formulas. It performs bidirectional conversions between hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, and annual rates while accounting for variables like standard work hours (e.g., 40-hour weeks), overtime multipliers (1.5x/2x rates), and prorated adjustments for partial periods. Technically, it calculates equivalent salaries using annualization formulas (e.g., hourly_rate × 2080 annual hours) and inverse operations for reverse conversions. Users need this for accurate financial modeling when comparing job offers with different pay structures, calculating contractor retainers, or aligning payroll systems across international offices with varying pay periods. The backend uses floating-point arithmetic with 15-digit precision to handle fractional currency values and supports optional adjustments for tax brackets, benefits deductions, and state-specific overtime rules through toggle switches. Results include both gross and net estimates based on configurable withholdings, with debug mode showing the exact calculation steps for transparency.
usage_steps: 1. Select input pay period from the dropdown (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly/annual)
2. Enter numeric salary value in the primary input field (e.g., 75.50)
3. Activate optional parameters via checkboxes: include overtime (1.5x), bonuses, or deductions
4. Choose target output period using the conversion direction arrows (→) between period buttons
5. Adjust work calendar settings: specify weekly hours, holidays, or leap year status if needed
6. Click 'Calculate' to execute conversion and view formula-derived results with 2-decimal currency precision
usage_examples: A freelance developer converts $45/hour (40 hrs/wk) to annual salary, including 10% overtime pay for 12 weeks/year
An HR manager calculates monthly equivalent of a $98,000 annual package with 25% tax withholdings
A part-time worker compares $18.75/hour (25 hrs/wk) vs a $36,000/year full-time offer including benefits
A startup founder converts 150 contracted hours/month to annual FTE cost including 30% overhead for benefits
